name: Made-in-India Shipping Containers: CMPS Scheme & Import Substitution
scope: India imports nearly all of its ~2 million empty containers a year (domestic output ~24-70k TEU, <5% of need) and the Union Cabinet approved the Rs 10,000 cr Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme on 28 Oct 2026 (3% interest subvention, per-box opex support, 70% local-content rule, 1 lakh TEU greenfield / 25k TEU brownfield thresholds); confirmed listed participants are few and mostly small line items (Kalyani Cast-Tech, DCM Shriram via DCM Shriram International, Mazagon Dock, BHEL unverified), so it is a narrow, fresh-policy theme, partly discovered (Kalyani already ~2.5x off its 52-week low and named in Feb 2026 'container stocks' pieces) with scheme guidelines and first scheme-scale plant announcements still to come.
questions: What is the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme (approved 28 Oct 2026): outlay, components (Rs 859 cr interest subvention, Rs 8,891 cr opex assistance, Rs 150 cr common testing), eligibility thresholds (1 lakh TEU greenfield, 25k TEU brownfield), 70% local-content rule, FY28-FY40 timeline, and what guidelines remain to be issued?

How big is India's container import dependence (~2 million empty boxes a year vs ~24-70k TEU domestic output), what is the cost gap versus China (roughly Rs 1.5-2 lakh vs Rs 3.5-4 lakh per 40ft box) and can subsidies plus steel/coupler localisation close it?

What has Kalyani Cast-Tech actually built in containers (13,000+ boxes since 2021, 6,000 to 16,000 TEU expansion plan, reefers), what is the current status of that capacity, and how large is containers versus wagons, castings and its logistics/terminal build-out?

What is DCM Shriram's real exposure through DCM Shriram International: the first Indian-made EXIM-grade box for Maersk (Dadri, 3 Jul 2026), the company's 6 Jul 2026 denial of a reported 1,000-unit Maersk order, and its capacity and capex intentions under CMPS?

Which other listed names have confirmed container activity (Mazagon Dock's 2022 CONCOR order for 2,500 boxes, BHEL and Braithwaite as earlier PSU entrants, any private steel/fabrication group planning a 1 lakh TEU plant) and which have only been loosely attributed in media pieces without company evidence?

Who could be the scale greenfield applicants (1 lakh TEU needs Rs several hundred crore plus corten steel, paint and flooring supply chain), and are there any exchange filings, board approvals or rating-agency rationales since 28 Oct 2026 announcing a CMPS-linked plant?

Can Indian makers compete with CIMC/Dong Fang/Singamas (~95% of global output) on quality, certification and delivery, and what do shipping lines (Maersk, others) and CONCOR say about offtake commitments?

Has the market already priced it in: Kalyani Cast-Tech's move (about Rs 440 low to ~Rs 1,150, 52-week high ~Rs 1,404), DCM Shriram's performance (down ~15% over a year), and how much 'container stocks' media/broker coverage exists so far?

What are the key risks: containers being a tiny share of revenue for most names, dependence on subsidy guideline details and 3-year commissioning deadlines, cyclical container prices, Chinese price undercutting, steel cost and local-content compliance?

What are the near-term catalysts: CMPS guidelines and steering-committee approvals, first sanctioned projects, shipping-line or CONCOR order announcements, and company capex disclosures in Q2 FY27 results?

container_makers: Listed companies already building or expanding shipping/cargo container production in India
psu_fabricators: Large caps with a past or small container line, where it is a minor part of the business
